subject: black fire beetle
title: This Beetle Flies Toward Wildfires It May Sense 80 Miles Away

scenes.text: Every animal runs from a forest fire. One beetle flies straight toward it.
Fire beetles swarm into burnt forests while the wood is still smoking.
They find fires with two tiny pits, each packed with about 70 infrared sensors.
In 1925, a burning oil tank in California drew swarms. Most probably flew about 80 miles to reach it.
The reason is their young. The larvae grow in trees freshly killed by fire.
With predators gone, the fire they chased becomes the safest nursery around.

description:
While other animals flee a wildfire, Melanophila fire beetles fly toward it.
The beetles carry two infrared pit organs on their thorax, each with about 70 heat-sensing sensilla. In 1925 an oil-tank fire in Coalinga, California, attracted huge numbers of them, and researchers estimate most came from the Sierra Nevada foothills about 130 km (80 miles) away. Their larvae develop in fire-killed trees, so the adults mate and lay eggs in fresh burns, where predators have fled.
Which animal sense would you most like to have?
first_comment: Scientists think these beetles cannot breed successfully in unburnt trees at all. Which animal sense would you steal?
